subject: Partial-path latency spike 2028-03-14 — ledger reconciliation request
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudbridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: noc@cloudbridge.com
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Partial degradation observed 2028-03-14 — request for ledger adjustment

Hi Rishi,

We noticed a sustained p95 latency increase for a subset of paths to your edge fleet between 03:21–03:29 UTC on 2028-03-14. Our monitoring and the attached probe dump (cloudbridge_probe_patch_20280314.csv) show a clear correlation with a planned peering maintenance we ran at 03:25 UTC. Several of our transit peers briefly withdrew routes, which forced re-pathing through an alternate transit that added ~120–180ms on affected paths.

CloudBridge believes this should be considered an upstream/third-party maintenance event for Redwood's SLA ledger (i.e., exclude or apportion impact accordingly). Can you confirm Redwood's position and provide the ledger entries used to compute availability for that window? If possible, we would like a ledger reconciliation and a statement of whether a credit will be applied or if Redwood attributes this to our transit maintenance.

I've attached our probe CSV and a link to the NOC announcement we posted. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Sr. Network Reliability Engineer — CloudBridge
Lena.ortiz@cloudbridge.com
Attachment: cloudbridge_probe_patch_20280314.csv
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partial degradation observed 2028-03-14 — request for ledger adjustment

Lena —

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the probe dump. We reviewed the initial telemetry and see the same spike in tail latency on the RedEdge-12 pool between 03:20–03:31 UTC. A few quick asks so we can reconcile cleanly:

- Can you point to the exact NOC post/ticket that documents the planned peering maintenance (we got a terse bulletin but no ticket id).
- Do you have traceroutes from an affected origin to our anycast IPs during the window (the CSV is helpful but we need path-level hops to attribute transit re-route).
- Did CloudBridge run a maintenance update that changed BGP community / local-pref during that minute?

From Redwood's side, our ledgering logic attempts to apportion partial degradations across origin-paths based on probe coverage and trace divergence. If the transit provider initiated an intentional route withdrawal that caused the re-pathing, we typically classify that as an upstream outage and exclude it from our primary uptime tally, but we need cross-corroborating traces.

CCing Marissa and Jonas to pull the ledger slice for the RedEdge-12 pool and to suggest next steps.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account SRE — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudbridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudBridge NOC <noc@cloudbridge.com>, TransitOps <ops@transitops.net>
Date: 2028-03-16T02:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partial degradation observed 2028-03-14 — request for ledger adjustment

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the quick reply. NOC post and ticket attached (noc_announcements_20280314.html) and traceroutes are in the PCAP (rfc_traceroutes_20280314.pcap). Summary:

- Maintenance job CB-MNT-20280314-PEER updated local-pref for two transit neighbors at 03:24:58 UTC and withdrew a route advertisement from TR-IX at 03:25:10 UTC.
- Our probes show path divergence at hop 4 that persists for ~6 minutes before BGP reconvergence.
- We did not intentionally change communities besides the maintenance action; ops ticket NETOPS-7642 documents the exact change.

We are amenable to a quick joint review. Our position is that this qualifies as a CloudBridge maintenance impacting Redwood traffic; we request exclusion or proportional apportionment per your SLA rules.

Lena
Attachment: noc_announcements_20280314.html; rfc_traceroutes_20280314.pcap
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudbridge.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partial degradation observed 2028-03-14 — request for ledger adjustment

Rishi / Lena —

We pulled the RedEdge-12 ledger slice and ran a differential on probe coverage. Quick read: the impacted session set maps to ~11% of total requests to that pool during the window; latency increased primarily on origin prefixes that routable via CloudBridge transit. Based on our SLA handbook the appropriate approach here is:

1) Collect hop-level traceroutes from CloudBridge (we have PCAP but need labelled traceroutes from your vantage).
2) We'll run our path-diff algorithm — if path divergence is caused by an upstream intentional withdraw, we mark the event as third-party-maintenance.
3) If confirmed, Redwood proposes a proportional ledger adjustment: exclude the fraction attributable to the transit-induced re-route (not a full incident credit for the account unless Redwood's own systems contributed).

Operational ask: Lena, can you push one more artifact — traceroutes with timestamps tied to your probe rows (hop-by-hop) and confirm NETOPS-7642 as the authoritative ticket? If we get those, Redwood can ship a reconciliation report within 48 hours.

Separately, Jonas and I discussed a one-time goodwill credit offer (covering 30% of the calculated apportionment) to shorten the negotiation window if CloudBridge confirms the maintenance window quickly. We'll wait on your trace artifacts before applying anything.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Reliability Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-22T17:38:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed mutual action plan and ledger reconciliation

Lena —

Thanks for the trace artifacts via Drive and for confirming NETOPS-7642. Per Marissa's note, next steps we propose:

- CloudBridge: provide hop-labelled traceroutes for the three example prefixes in the PCAP (timestamps in UTC).
- Redwood: produce a ledger reconciliation report showing total request counts, affected fraction, and the apportioned exclusion (expected delivery: 48 hours after receipt of traceroutes).
- If CloudBridge confirms the maintenance was intentional and matches the traces, Redwood will mark the event as third-party-maintenance and apply a proportional ledger correction. Given the timeline, Marissa has pre-authorized a one-time goodwill credit equal to 30% of the apportioned impact to accelerate closure; this will appear as an adjustment on the next billing cycle pending final reconciliation.

Please confirm the action items and whether CloudBridge is comfortable with the proposed 48-hour turnaround. If yes, attach the traceroutes in the same Drive folder and we'll begin the reconciliation run. For approvals, I've included a short DocuSign form we use to accept mutually-agreed credits: https://docusign.redwood.com/CB-20280314-credit-accept

If you prefer a huddle, I'm available tomorrow morning PST.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account SRE — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Attachment: proposed_reconciliation_parameters.txt
